en.title: 자기소개
question: Tell me about yourself. What do you do, and what do you enjoy outside work?
answer: I'm a physician from Korea, and my specialty is family medicine. These days, I work at Kakao Healthcare, where I help develop AI tools for doctors. A big part of my job is explaining what happens in a clinic to people who build software.

Before this, I spent about seven years living and working in China. That experience made me more comfortable working with people from different backgrounds. It also gave me a reason to keep improving my Chinese.

Outside work, I've recently taken up tennis. I'm still a beginner, so I have plenty to learn. I'm also interested in investing and learning Python. My schedule is busy, but I like having something new to work on. It keeps life interesting.

en.title: 현재 업무를 쉽게 설명하기
question: Describe your current job. What do you actually do?
answer: I work on AI tools for electronic health records. That's the software doctors use to check a patient's history and write notes. My role is to help the team understand which information really matters in a medical setting.

For example, before seeing a returning patient, a doctor may need to know what has changed since the last visit. Has a test result become worse? Has the medication changed? I help turn questions like those into features that engineers and designers can build.

I work with several different teams, so communication takes up a lot of my time. My title includes Clinical Intelligence Lead, but in everyday terms, I'm someone who connects clinical experience with product development. I find that rewarding because a small improvement on a screen can make a busy doctor's day easier.
vocab: turn a problem into a feature

en.title: 평일의 하루
question: Walk me through a typical weekday, from morning to evening.
answer: A typical weekday starts with checking my schedule. I like to know which meetings need preparation and which decisions I need to make. If I have a little time, I also read news about healthcare or AI.

During the day, I move between discussions with medical, product, and engineering teams. Sometimes the topic is quite detailed, like what a doctor should see at the top of a patient's record. Other times, we discuss the direction of a whole service. Switching between those levels can be tiring.

In the evening, I try to leave room for family and some movement. That might mean tennis, stretching, or simply a short walk. I don't manage a perfect routine every day. If work runs late, I keep things simple and try again the next day.

en.title: 기억에 남는 음성 차팅 프로젝트
question: Tell me about a project that has been especially meaningful to you.
answer: One project that stands out is an AI tool that helps turn a medical conversation into a draft note. Doctors spend a lot of time documenting visits, so this is a very practical problem.

The difficult part is that a consultation isn't a neat speech. A patient may stop halfway through a sentence, change the subject, or mention a medicine without remembering its name. We need to think about how the system handles those moments. We also need a way for the doctor to review and correct the draft.

I'm involved in thinking through those clinical situations and how to evaluate the tool. The work has reminded me that an impressive demonstration isn't the same as a reliable product. What matters is whether it helps during an ordinary, busy clinic day. That's the question I keep coming back to.

en.title: 팀의 의견 차이를 해결한 경험
question: Tell me about a time people disagreed at work. How did you help?
answer: I remember a discussion about a patient summary screen. One group wanted more information on the screen, while another wanted a simpler layout. We kept saying things like 'important' and 'easy to use,' but those words meant different things to different people.

I suggested walking through one returning patient's visit. We asked what the doctor needed before entering the room and what could wait until later. Once we used that concrete example, the discussion became easier. We separated the key changes from the extra details.

The team was then able to discuss a clearer design. What I took away was that disagreement doesn't always mean people have conflicting goals. Sometimes they're imagining different situations. A specific example can help everyone talk about the same thing.

en.title: 의료의 과거와 현재
question: How has healthcare changed since you started your career?
answer: When I started working as a doctor, most of the information I used came from hospital visits. We saw a patient, checked the available results, and made a plan. That is still important, but we now have more information from everyday life.

A good example is continuous glucose monitoring. Instead of seeing just one blood sugar result, we can look at changes over time, including what happens after meals or exercise. My work in digital healthcare has made me especially interested in that difference.

However, more data doesn't automatically make care better. Someone has to explain what the numbers mean and which changes deserve attention. I think that's where both clinicians and technology have useful roles. The biggest change, for me, is being able to see a longer story rather than a single moment.

en.title: 중국에서 보낸 약 7년
question: Tell me about your experience living in another country.
answer: I spent about seven years living and working in China, with experience in places such as Shanghai, Suzhou, and Wuxi. It was a substantial part of my career, rather than a short overseas assignment.

At first, I had to learn much more than vocabulary. I needed to understand how colleagues explained problems, how hospitals operated, and how to build trust with people I had just met. Knowing medicine was useful, but it wasn't enough on its own.

Over time, I became more willing to ask questions instead of assuming that my usual approach would work everywhere. That has stayed with me since returning to Korea. When I work with a new team now, I try to understand their situation before offering a solution. Living in China made me a more flexible colleague and gave me a much wider view of healthcare.

en.title: 중국 정착 초기의 작은 어려움
question: Describe a problem you had when you first moved abroad.
answer: One difficulty I had after moving to China was setting up mobile payment. I understood the basic idea but got stuck during registration. The screen asked for information I wasn't sure how to enter, and I couldn't complete the process.

At first, I tried to solve it by translating each word. That didn't really help because I still didn't understand the whole procedure. So I asked a colleague to walk me through it. We checked the details step by step, and I wrote down the important terms.

Once it was working, buying small things became much easier. The lesson I learned was simple: when you're settling into a new country, asking for help can save a lot of time. You don't have to understand everything on your own from day one.

en.title: 한국과 중국의 업무 경험 비교
question: Compare your work experience in Korea with your experience in China.
answer: I noticed some differences, although I wouldn't say everyone in either country works the same way. In some of the teams I worked with in China, people were very willing to try an idea quickly and adjust it after getting feedback.

In other settings, including some of my experience in Korea, we spent more time agreeing on the details before moving forward. Both approaches can be useful. A quick trial can reveal a problem early, while careful preparation can prevent avoidable mistakes.

Because I work in healthcare, I can't simply choose speed in every situation. For a screen layout, a small trial might be reasonable. For something that could affect clinical decisions, the checks need to be much stricter. My experience in both countries taught me to match the approach to the problem rather than assume one style is always better.

en.title: 외국어 오해를 풀었던 장면
question: Tell me about a misunderstanding caused by language and how it was resolved.
answer: I once misunderstood a delivery date during a meeting. I heard that a task would be ready 'soon' and assumed that meant the same week. Later, I realized the other person hadn't promised a specific date.

I felt a little awkward because I had already started planning the next step. Instead of blaming anyone, I asked a more precise question: 'Do you mean this Friday, or sometime next week?' Then I repeated the agreed date and sent a short written summary.

That situation shows why understanding individual words isn't enough. You also need to check what people have actually agreed to. In an international team, I think a simple confirmation can be more useful than trying to sound perfectly fluent. I'd rather ask one extra question than leave with the wrong idea.

en.title: 기억에 남는 도시 우시
question: Tell me about a city that is meaningful to you. Why do you remember it?
answer: Wuxi is a city that means a lot to me because an important part of my career took place there. I worked in an international medical center, so my connection with the city is mainly about everyday life and work, rather than sightseeing.

When I think of Wuxi, I think about learning how to run a healthcare service in a different environment. I had to consider patients' expectations, how a team worked together, and how ideas could become practical services. Those experiences pushed me beyond my original role as a doctor.

I'd like to go back and see how the city and the people I knew have changed. I imagine it would feel familiar and unfamiliar at the same time. For me, a memorable city isn't always the one with the most famous attractions. Sometimes it's the place where you learned the most.

en.title: 영어 중국어를 함께 공부하는 이유
question: What languages are you learning, and how do you plan to improve?
answer: I'm working on both English and Chinese. English is useful for reading research and discussing technology, while Chinese connects with the years I spent living and working in China. I don't want to lose that ability simply because I use it less often now.

My plan is to prepare the same personal stories in both languages. For example, I can talk about my job, tennis, or my time abroad. That way, I don't have to invent a new story every time I switch languages.

Still, I don't want to translate every sentence word for word. I want each version to sound natural. I'll use a few keywords, record myself, and check where I get stuck. Short, regular sessions seem more realistic for me than waiting for a completely free afternoon. The aim is to express my own ideas more comfortably.
vocab: fit something into a busy schedule

en.title: 2027년 박사과정 진학
question: Tell me about an important plan for your education or career.
answer: I've been accepted into a PhD program at KAIST, and I plan to begin in 2027. My interest is in AI and healthcare. I also plan to keep working, so managing my time will be a serious challenge.

The reason I want to study again is that I keep running into questions that practical experience alone can't fully answer. For instance, how can we turn complicated medical records into information that actually helps a doctor? I want stronger research skills to investigate questions like that.

I'm looking forward to being a student again, although I know it won't be easy. I'll need to protect time for reading, technical study, and research. I don't see the degree as the end of my career path. I see it as a way to connect my clinical and business experience with a deeper understanding of AI.
vocab: have been accepted into a program

en.title: 초보자로서 Python 배우기
question: Tell me about a new skill you are learning. What is difficult about it?
answer: I'm a beginner at Python. My long-term goal is to use it for data analysis, especially when I study companies or investment ideas. I'd also like to understand technical discussions at work more directly.

The challenge is that knowing what you want to analyze is different from knowing how to write the code. A small error can stop everything, and the message on the screen may look confusing. I need to be patient and work through one step at a time.

A realistic starting point for me is a simple table: load the data, calculate a few values, and make a clear chart. I haven't become an expert overnight, and I don't expect to. What attracts me is the possibility of checking an idea for myself instead of depending entirely on someone else's analysis.

en.title: 취미로서 투자 공부
question: What do you enjoy learning about in your free time?
answer: I enjoy learning about investing. Making money is certainly part of the attraction, but I also like understanding why some industries grow while others struggle. It gives me a practical reason to study how the world is changing.

I pay particular attention to AI, semiconductors, and healthcare. When a technology sounds promising, I try to ask what customers will actually pay for and how a company can earn a profit. A good story and a good business aren't always the same thing.

The difficult part is dealing with uncertainty. You can study a company carefully and still be wrong. So I try to separate what I know from what I'm assuming. I wouldn't describe investing as a relaxing hobby all the time, but it keeps me curious and makes me question my own judgment.

en.title: 최근 깊이 살펴본 산업
question: Tell me about a topic you have recently spent time researching.
answer: Recently, I've been interested in the shipbuilding industry. It may sound far removed from medicine, but I like topics where technology, business, and global trade come together.

One question I've been exploring is what happens when many older ships need replacing but shipyards can't immediately build more vessels. Strong demand is only one part of the picture. You also have to think about production capacity, delivery times, costs, and changing environmental requirements. That makes the subject more complicated than a simple growth story.

I like to compare several possible outcomes rather than rely on a single forecast. What if demand stays strong? What if orders slow down? I haven't reached a final answer, and that's part of the interest. Researching something outside my own profession reminds me how much I still have to learn.

en.title: 읽고 싶은 역사책과 독서 습관
question: What kinds of books interest you? Tell me about one you would like to read.
answer: I'm interested in books that help me understand how people and societies change. History is especially appealing because it gives me a longer perspective than daily news.

One book I'd like to spend more time with is The Lessons of History by Will and Ariel Durant. I've been interested in its broad questions about human behavior and social change. I wouldn't claim that history gives us a precise formula for predicting the future, but it can make today's events look less isolated.

Because my schedule is busy, I don't always have time for a long reading session. A practical approach for me is to read a small section and write down one question. Then I can connect that question with something in my work or investment research. I want reading to change how I think, not just add more titles to a list.

en.title: 앞으로 5년의 목표
question: Where would you like to be in five years?
answer: In five years, I'd like to have a stronger connection between my experience as a doctor and my work in AI. I've worked in clinical care, healthcare services in China, and digital health in Korea. Now I want those experiences to lead to something more coherent.

One goal is to make meaningful progress in my doctoral research. Another is to help create tools that doctors choose to use because they actually solve a problem. I'd be more proud of a service that improves everyday work than a presentation that simply sounds impressive.

I also want to stay healthy enough to enjoy the process. My interest in tennis and endurance sports is part of that. I know plans can change, so I'm not attached to a particular title. What matters to me is continuing to learn and becoming someone who can connect different fields effectively.

en.title: 최근 시작한 테니스
question: What sport have you recently become interested in? Describe it in detail.
answer: I've recently become interested in tennis. I started in the summer of 2026, so I'm still very much a beginner. What I like is that it forces me to focus on what's happening right in front of me.

At work, I often have several problems in my head at once. On a tennis court, the next ball demands my attention. Even a basic rally involves timing, footwork, and controlling how hard I hit. It's more demanding than it looks when I watch experienced players.

I've also looked for places where I could practice against a wall. That seems useful when I don't have a partner. I don't expect to become good immediately. For now, I'd be happy to make steadier contact with the ball and move more comfortably. Small improvements are enough to keep me interested.

en.title: 첫 테니스 레슨의 작은 깨달음
question: Tell me about a memorable experience while learning a sport.
answer: One memorable experience was an early tennis lesson. I was trying to hit the ball harder because I thought power would make the shot better. Instead, the ball kept going in the wrong direction, and I was getting frustrated.

The coach asked me to slow down and pay attention to my feet. I took a smaller swing and tried to get into position earlier. After a few attempts, I managed a short, steady rally. It wasn't an impressive shot, but it felt much better than hitting one hard ball and missing the next three.

I remember feeling relieved because I finally had one clear thing to work on. That is the lesson I'd take from the experience: when you're a beginner, doing a simple thing consistently is often more useful than trying to look advanced. I can apply that to language learning as well.

en.title: 운동 습관의 변화
question: How have your exercise habits changed over time?
answer: My attitude toward exercise has changed. I used to focus more on how hard a workout felt. Now I pay more attention to whether I can recover well and keep exercising over the long term.

I'm interested in running, cycling, swimming, and tennis, but I also think about mobility and basic strength. If one movement doesn't feel right, I don't want to ignore it just to complete a plan. As a doctor, I understand the general value of exercise, but turning that knowledge into a sensible personal routine still takes effort.

My ideal session doesn't have to be long. On a busy day, a shorter activity can be worthwhile. What I want is a routine I can return to, even after a difficult week. For me, the real change has been moving from chasing one hard workout to building a habit that lasts.

en.title: 무릎 불편과 운동 계획 조정
question: Describe a difficulty that affected your exercise plans.
answer: One difficulty has been discomfort and a feeling of instability in my right knee during certain movements. It's frustrating because I want to stay active and try different sports, but I also need to pay attention to how my body responds.

It made me think more carefully about movement quality. Simply asking whether I can finish a workout isn't enough. I also need to notice which movements cause trouble and whether I'm recovering properly. I've become more interested in mobility, rehabilitation, and how different parts of the body work together.

I wouldn't say everything is completely resolved. What has changed is my approach. I'm more willing to adjust a plan instead of forcing myself through it. That's not always easy when I'm motivated, but I'd rather make steady progress than let one ambitious session interrupt my activities for a long time.

en.title: 철인3종 도전 목표
question: What physical challenge would you like to try in the future?
answer: I'd like to work toward a triathlon. I haven't completed one, so this is a goal rather than an achievement. What appeals to me is the combination of swimming, cycling, and running. You need more than one kind of fitness, and you have to manage your energy.

The biggest challenge for me would be fitting preparation around work and family. I couldn't train as if I were a professional athlete. I'd need a realistic schedule and enough room to recover, especially when my body isn't feeling quite right.

I would start by building consistency in the separate activities instead of rushing to enter an event. Even if it takes longer than I first expect, I think the process would be valuable. Having a clear physical goal gives me another reason to protect time for health in a busy life.

en.title: 가민과 건강 데이터
question: Tell me about a device or app you use to understand your daily life.
answer: I'm interested in the information from my Garmin device, especially exercise, sleep, and recovery-related data. Since I work in digital healthcare, I naturally want to understand what those numbers can and can't tell me.

For example, I might want to compare how I feel after a busy week with what the device shows. Am I sleeping less? Do I feel tired even when I want to exercise? The data can give me a reason to stop and pay attention, but I don't want one number to make every decision for me.

I think the useful part is noticing patterns over time. The less useful part is becoming anxious whenever a score changes. I want technology to help me understand my habits, while still leaving room for common sense and how I actually feel. Otherwise, tracking health can become another source of stress.

en.title: 가족과 보내는 평범한 시간
question: Tell me about your family and the time you spend together.
answer: My family is the part of my life that brings me back to ordinary things. At work, I spend a lot of time discussing complicated projects. At home, the conversation might be about school, a meal, or something funny that happened during the day.

I don't think every family moment needs a special plan. Having dinner together and listening properly can be enough. The hard part is giving my full attention when I'm still thinking about work. I try to remind myself that being in the same room isn't quite the same as being present.

As a parent, I want my children to see that learning doesn't stop when you become an adult. If they see me struggling with tennis or learning something new, that's probably a more honest example than acting as if I already know everything.

en.title: 아이의 진로 이야기를 듣기
question: Tell me about an interesting conversation with a family member.
answer: A topic I've found interesting is my daughter's interest in becoming a diplomat. She spent part of her childhood in China, so international life isn't just something she knows from a textbook. It connects with her own experience.

When we talk about her future, I try to ask what attracts her to that work. Is it understanding different cultures, representing her country, or helping people communicate? I don't want the conversation to be only about getting into a particular school.

Her interests have also reminded me that a child's plans can develop over time. My role isn't to decide everything for her. I want to help her connect experiences, books, and questions in a thoughtful way. Sometimes listening to how she explains an idea teaches me more than giving another piece of advice would.

en.title: 집과 좋아하는 공간
question: Describe your home. Which part of it do you like best?
answer: I live in an apartment with my family. The part I like best is a quiet corner where I can sit with my laptop and read. It isn't a dramatic space, but it helps me switch from a busy workday to something I can do at my own pace.

I imagine the ideal setup as a simple desk, a comfortable chair, and enough light. I don't need many decorations. What matters more is being able to find what I need without moving piles of things around. If the space is too cluttered, I find it harder to concentrate.

I also like that home isn't just a workplace. I can step away from the screen, talk with my family, and come back later if necessary. That balance is what makes the space comfortable for me: a little room to think, but still a connection with the people around me.

en.title: 이상적인 주말
question: What would an ideal weekend look like for you?
answer: An ideal weekend would have one active part and one quiet part. I'd like to start with some exercise, perhaps tennis or a relaxed bike ride, without feeling that I have to rush straight into a meeting afterward.

Later, I'd enjoy a meal with my family and some time when nobody has to follow a strict schedule. We wouldn't need to travel far. Even a simple outing can feel different when we're not checking the time constantly. I might also leave an hour for reading or studying a topic that interests me.

The main thing is that I wouldn't fill every gap with another task. I can easily turn free time into a second work schedule. A good weekend, for me, would leave me feeling both physically refreshed and mentally less crowded by Sunday evening.

en.title: 집에서 인터넷이 끊긴 날
question: Tell me about a problem you had at home and how you handled it.
answer: One morning, the internet stopped working just before an online meeting. At first, I thought it was only my laptop, but my phone couldn't connect to the Wi-Fi either.

I restarted the router and waited, but the connection didn't return in time. So I sent a short message to the team and used my phone's mobile connection as a temporary backup. The video quality wasn't ideal, but I could hear the discussion and take part in the important decisions.

After the meeting, I contacted the provider and checked what needed to be done. What I learned was to separate the immediate problem from the underlying one. First, I needed to join the meeting. Then I could deal with the connection properly. Trying to fix everything at once would probably have made me miss the whole conversation.

en.title: 동네 산책 공간
question: Describe an outdoor place near your home where people can relax.
answer: A place near my home is a walking path beside a stream. It has a fairly open view, a route for walking, and space where people can move at different speeds. It feels much less hectic than a busy street.

In the evening, you might see someone jogging, a couple walking slowly, or a parent spending time with a child. I like places where people don't need to spend money or organize anything complicated just to enjoy being outside.

For me, the appeal is the change of pace. After looking at screens and talking in meetings, walking along water gives me something simple to focus on. I don't need a challenging workout every time. Sometimes the best use of a nearby outdoor space is just to move a little and let the day settle.
vocab: a walking path beside a stream

en.title: 편하게 가는 식당
question: Describe a restaurant you enjoy. What is it like, and why do you go there?
answer: The kind of restaurant I enjoy is a simple Korean place where I can have a comfortable meal with family or colleagues. It's a small restaurant serving soup, rice, and a few side dishes. The tables aren't fancy, but the room is bright and the service is straightforward.

I'd usually choose something familiar, especially after a long day. I don't always want to study a huge menu or wait in line for a popular dish. What matters is being able to sit down, enjoy the food, and hear the person across from me.

A restaurant like that may not look exciting in a photograph, but it serves a real purpose in daily life. If everyone leaves feeling comfortable and we have a good conversation, I consider that a successful meal out.
vocab: hear the person across from me

en.title: 직접 간단히 요리한 경험
question: Tell me about a time you prepared a meal. What happened?
answer: I remember making fried rice at home. I had some rice, eggs, and vegetables, and I thought it would be an easy way to put a meal together without using too many dishes.

I chopped the vegetables and put almost everything into the pan at once. That was my mistake. There was too much moisture, so the rice became softer than I wanted. I lowered my expectations, let some of the moisture cook off, and focused on getting the seasoning right. The result was edible, even if it wasn't restaurant quality.

What made the experience enjoyable was how different it felt from work. I could see the result immediately and learn one practical lesson: the order matters. Next time, I'd cook the ingredients in stages and keep the meal simple.

en.title: 좋아하는 카페의 조건
question: What makes a café a place you would want to visit again?
answer: For me, a café needs to be comfortable enough that I don't want to leave immediately. Good coffee matters, but so do the chairs, the noise level, and whether it's easy to have a conversation.

I've become more interested in this because I've been thinking about possible uses for a property in Yangpyeong that previously had a café. That makes me look at cafés from a visitor's point of view as well as a business point of view. Can people find the entrance easily? Is there a reason to return after taking a photo once?

Personally, I'd rather have a calm place with a clear purpose than a beautiful room that feels inconvenient. If I can sit comfortably, talk without raising my voice, and leave in a better mood, the café has done its job.
vocab: from a visitor’s point of view

en.title: 온라인 쇼핑 전후 비교
question: How has shopping changed, and how do you decide what to buy?
answer: Shopping is much easier now in terms of finding information. Before going anywhere, I can compare products, read descriptions, and check whether the price fits my budget. That is useful when I don't have much free time.

For something like sports equipment, though, a long list of positive reviews isn't enough. I want to know whether the size, weight, and purpose match my needs. As a beginner at tennis, for example, buying the most expensive item wouldn't automatically make it the right choice.

I also pay attention to return conditions, especially if I can't try the item first. The drawback of online shopping is that convenience makes it easy to buy too quickly. I try to pause and ask whether the purchase solves a real problem. Sometimes the most useful decision is to wait until I understand what I actually need.

en.title: 교통수단 선택과 지각 경험
question: Tell me about a time transportation caused a problem for you.
answer: I once got caught in traffic on the way to a meeting, even though I thought I had allowed enough time. I had checked the route, but the journey took longer than expected, and I realized I might miss the beginning of the meeting.

The first thing I did was send a message with a realistic arrival estimate. I didn't want everyone waiting without knowing what was happening. I also asked whether the team could begin with an item that didn't need my input. That helped reduce the inconvenience, even though I still felt bad about being late.

After that, I decided to build in a larger buffer for important appointments and consider public transport when the travel time is easier to predict. The main lesson is that, once a delay is unavoidable, clear communication is more useful than repeatedly hoping the traffic will suddenly disappear.

en.title: 재활용과 작은 생활 습관
question: Tell me about recycling or another household habit. Has it changed?
answer: A household habit worth talking about is sorting waste. With deliveries and online shopping, it's easy for packaging to build up. Even a small purchase can leave a box, some plastic, and extra wrapping to deal with.

I check what the material is, empty the container, and separate it according to the local guidance. The annoying part is packaging made from several materials, because it's not always obvious what should go where. I wouldn't assume the rules are exactly the same in every neighborhood.

I think the better starting point is reducing unnecessary packaging when possible. Sorting matters, but having less to throw away makes the whole task easier. For me, this is a good example of a small habit that isn't exciting on its own but becomes meaningful when people do it consistently.

en.title: 가족과 다시 가보고 싶은 중국
question: Where would you like to travel with your family, and what would you do there?
answer: I'd like to revisit China with my family. Since we spent an important part of our lives there, the trip would be more than just seeing famous attractions. It would be a chance to reconnect with places that were once part of our ordinary routine.

I'd prefer to choose a small number of places rather than rush between several cities. We could walk around an area we remember, have a meal, and talk about what feels the same or different. I'd also leave room for my children to choose something, because their memories may be different from mine.

What would make the trip meaningful is the conversation. A familiar street might bring back a story we haven't discussed for years. I don't have a fixed itinerary yet, but I like the idea of a trip that connects our past experience with who we are now.

en.title: 출장과 가족 여행 준비의 차이
question: How do you prepare for a trip? Is a business trip different from a family trip?
answer: For a business trip, I'd start with the things that would be difficult to replace at the last minute: identification, travel details, essential documents, and the equipment I need for work. A laptop without its charger isn't very useful, so I'd check those small items carefully.

For a family trip, I'd think more about the pace of the day. I'd want everyone to know the main plan, but I wouldn't schedule something for every hour. A meal taking longer than expected shouldn't ruin the whole afternoon.

In both cases, I'd keep important information easy to find and leave some room for a change of plan. The difference is the purpose. A work trip needs to support a particular task. A family trip should give us time together. I don't want to prepare so many activities that the holiday starts to feel like another project.
vocab: leave room for a change of plan

en.title: 비 때문에 바뀐 운동 약속
question: Tell me about a time the weather changed your plans.
answer: I had planned to play tennis outdoors, but the weather turned worse than expected. The rain started lightly, so I kept hoping it would stop. Then it became clear that the court wouldn't be suitable for playing.

I was disappointed because I had been looking forward to some exercise after a busy week. I contacted the person I was meeting and suggested two options: move the session to another day or find an indoor activity instead. We decided to reschedule rather than spend the whole afternoon waiting for the weather.

Once the decision was made, I felt less frustrated. I could use the time for something else instead of checking the forecast again and again. It was a small reminder that flexibility matters. A changed plan doesn't have to mean a wasted day.

en.title: AI가 바꾼 정보 탐색
question: What technology has changed how you learn or work?
answer: AI has changed how I get started on a task. When I'm facing a large amount of information, it can help me organize the main questions or produce a first draft. That is useful for topics ranging from healthcare to language learning.

For example, I can take a personal story and explore how to express it naturally in English and Chinese. I can also ask for a simpler explanation of a technical concept before reading more deeply. It lowers the barrier to beginning something unfamiliar.

However, I still need to check important details. A smooth answer can contain an error, and the confidence of the wording doesn't tell me whether it is correct. So I treat the output as something to work with, not something to accept automatically. The biggest benefit is getting moving faster while keeping responsibility for the final result.

en.title: 편리함과 개인정보 사이
question: What concerns do you have about technology in daily life?
answer: One concern I have is that people can give away information without understanding why it's needed. A service may be convenient, but that doesn't mean every request for personal data is necessary.

Because I work in healthcare, I think about this particularly carefully. Health information can be deeply personal. If I were explaining a new service, I'd want people to understand what is being collected, what it will be used for, and what choices they have. A long page of difficult language wouldn't be enough for me.

I don't think we have to reject useful technology. I just want the benefit and the responsibility to be clear. Personally, I'd feel more comfortable with a service that asks for what it needs and explains the reason in plain language. Trust grows when people can understand the arrangement, rather than simply being asked to click a button.

en.title: 고령화와 지역 돌봄
question: What social issue are you interested in, and why?
answer: I'm interested in how we support older adults as a society. My medical background makes me think about treatment, but healthcare is only one part of daily life. Someone may also need help with meals, transport, or staying connected with other people.

I've been looking at care services as a possible area where clinical experience and technology could work together. For example, better communication between a family, a care team, and a clinic might reduce confusion when a person's condition changes. That sounds simple, but the information often sits in different places.

I don't think an app alone can solve the problem. People still need reliable services and human contact. What interests me is designing support around the person's whole day, not only around a hospital appointment. It's a subject I'd like to understand more deeply before deciding what kind of service could be useful.

en.title: 롤플레이 테니스장 문의
question: You want to try a tennis club. Call the club and ask three or four questions before making a booking.
answer: Hello, I'm interested in trying your tennis club. I'm a beginner, and I have a few questions before I book anything. First, do you offer lessons for people who have only recently started playing? I'd prefer a small group or a short individual session.

Also, what evening or weekend times are usually available? I work during the day, so it would help to know whether you have anything after work. Could you tell me whether I can rent a racket, or should I bring my own?

Finally, how much would a trial lesson cost, and is the court fee included? If it rains, would the lesson move indoors or be rescheduled? Thank you. Once I know the options, I can check my calendar and choose a time.

en.title: 롤플레이 테니스장 예약 불가 해결
question: You arrive for tennis, but your reserved court is unavailable. Explain the problem and suggest two alternatives.
answer: Hello, I booked a court for seven this evening, but I've just been told that it isn't available. I have the confirmation here. Could you check what happened? I've arranged my evening around this booking, so I'd appreciate your help finding a solution.

One option would be to move us to another court at the same time, if you have one nearby. If that's not possible, could we start a little later this evening without an extra charge? We could wait for a short time, but a very late session wouldn't work.

If neither option is available, I'd like to discuss rescheduling or getting a refund. I understand that problems happen. I mainly want to know what we can do now, and I'd appreciate written confirmation of whichever arrangement we agree on.

en.title: 롤플레이 병원 진료 예약
question: Call a clinic to arrange a nonurgent appointment. Ask about availability and what to bring.
answer: Hello, I'd like to ask about making an appointment. I've been having some knee discomfort during certain movements, and I'd like to have it checked. It isn't an emergency, but I'd appreciate an appointment when one is available.

Do you have any openings later this week? An evening appointment would be easiest because I work during the day. If evenings aren't available, could you tell me the earliest morning time you have? Also, which department or doctor would be appropriate for this kind of concern?

Could you let me know what I should bring, such as identification or previous examination records? I'd also like to know how early I should arrive for registration. Please let me know the available options first, and I'll choose a time that I can attend.

en.title: 롤플레이 병원 예약 변경
question: You have a clinic appointment, but a work meeting has been scheduled at the same time. Call and ask to change it.
answer: Hello, I'm calling about my appointment for Thursday at ten in the morning. I'm sorry, but a work meeting has been scheduled at the same time, and I won't be able to attend as planned.

Would it be possible to move the appointment to Thursday afternoon? If that isn't available, Friday morning would also work for me. I'd prefer to keep it within this week if possible, but I can discuss other options if the schedule is full. Could you check what is available?

Please also let me know whether there is a fee for changing the appointment at this point. I understand the clinic needs enough notice to manage its schedule. Once we find a new time, could you send me a confirmation? I want to make sure I update my calendar correctly. Thank you for your help.

en.title: 롤플레이 호텔 문의
question: You are considering a hotel for a family trip. Call and ask questions before booking.
answer: Hello, I'm planning a family trip and would like to ask a few questions about your hotel. We're considering a two-night stay. What room options would you suggest for a family? I'd like to understand the sleeping arrangements and the maximum number of guests before choosing.

Also, do you have rooms in a quieter part of the building? We don't need a special view, but we'd appreciate being able to rest comfortably. Is breakfast included in the room rate, or is it charged separately?

I'd also like to know how easy it is to reach the hotel by public transport. Finally, what would happen if our travel dates changed? Could you explain the cancellation deadline and any fees? Thank you. I'll compare the options and get back to you once our plans are confirmed.

en.title: 롤플레이 호텔 예약 누락
question: You arrive at a hotel, but the staff cannot find your reservation. Explain the problem and ask for a solution.
answer: Hello, I made a reservation in advance, but I've been told that it isn't showing in your system. I have the confirmation email on my phone. Could you check the name and dates against this message? We have just arrived, so I'd really appreciate your help.

If the original room isn't available, could you offer another room of a similar standard at the agreed rate? We're flexible about the exact room location, but we do need suitable sleeping arrangements for the family.

If you're fully booked, could you help us find a nearby hotel and explain how any difference in price would be handled? I understand there may have been a system problem. Right now, our priority is having a place to stay tonight. Could you tell me which option you can arrange and approximately how long it will take?
vocab: a room of a similar standard

en.title: 롤플레이 운동기기 반품 문의
question: A fitness device you bought does not charge. Call the store, explain the problem, and ask for a remedy.
answer: Hello, I'm calling about a fitness device I recently bought from your store. It doesn't seem to charge. I've checked the cable and tried another power source, but the device still won't turn on. I have the receipt and the original packaging.

Could you tell me what you need to check the problem? I can bring it to the store, or send a short video if that helps you understand what's happening. I'd prefer an exchange if you have the same model in stock.

If a replacement isn't available, I'd like to know whether a refund is possible. Please also explain whether I need to make an appointment before bringing it in and how long the process usually takes. I don't want to buy extra accessories until we know whether the original device is faulty. Thank you for checking.

en.title: 롤플레이 카페 모임 예약
question: You want to arrange a small gathering at a café. Call and ask about the space, cost, and booking conditions.
answer: Hello, I'm looking for a place for a small gathering, and I'd like to ask about your café. There would be about six people. Do you have a quieter area where we could sit together and talk without disturbing other customers?

We're considering a weekend afternoon. Is it possible to reserve a table, and would there be a time limit? Could you also explain whether there is a minimum order or a separate fee for reserving the space? We mainly want drinks and a comfortable place to talk.

A few people may arrive by car, so I'd like to know about parking as well. Is the entrance easy to find from the road? Finally, how far in advance should we confirm the booking? Once I have those details, I can coordinate with the group.

en.title: 롤플레이 친구와 약속 변경
question: You cannot keep a weekend plan with a friend. Leave a message explaining and suggesting alternatives.
answer: Hi, it's me. I'm sorry, but I need to change our plan for Saturday. Something important has come up at work, and I won't be free for the whole afternoon as we expected. I wanted to tell you now rather than leave it until the last minute.

Would you be interested in meeting for a shorter coffee in the morning instead? I could still make that work. If you'd rather keep the longer outing, we could move it to the following weekend. I'd understand either way, especially if you've already arranged other things around our plan.

Please let me know which option suits you better. I'm disappointed too because I was looking forward to catching up properly. Once we choose a new time, I'll put it in my calendar and make sure it's protected. Thanks for being flexible.

en.title: 롤플레이 강좌 등록 문의
question: You want to join a beginner coding course. Call the organizer and ask whether it suits you.
answer: Hello, I'm interested in your beginner Python course. I work full time and have very little coding experience, so I'd like to ask a few questions before registering. Does the course start from the basics, or should I already know some programming?

What days and times are the classes held? If I miss a session because of work, would a recording or another way to catch up be available? I'd also like to know roughly how much time I should allow for assignments each week.

My main interest is data analysis. Will we practice with simple tables and charts, or is the course focused on building websites? Finally, what software or equipment should I prepare? I want to choose something I can follow consistently, rather than join a course that's too advanced for me.
vocab: catch up on a missed session

en.title: 롤플레이 인터넷 장애 신고
question: Your home internet has stopped working. Call the provider and ask for help.
answer: Hello, I'm calling because my home internet isn't working. Both my laptop and my phone fail to connect, so it doesn't seem to be a problem with only one device. I've already restarted the router, but that hasn't solved it.

Could you check whether there's an outage in my area or an issue with my connection? I can provide my account details privately when you need them. I have work that depends on a stable connection, so I'd appreciate an estimate of when service might return.

If a technician needs to visit, what is the earliest appointment available? Also, is there any temporary option you can suggest while I wait? Before we finish, could you summarize the next step and how I'll receive updates? I want to make sure I don't miss a call or a message about the repair.

en.title: 롤플레이 취소 수수료 이견
question: You were charged a cancellation fee you did not expect. Call, explain your concern, and suggest a fair solution.
answer: Hello, I'm calling about a cancellation fee on my recent booking. I understand that you may have a cancellation policy, but I wasn't expecting this charge. Could you show me which condition applies and when it was explained during the booking process?

I'd appreciate it if you could review the timing of my cancellation as well. If the fee was applied incorrectly, I'd like it refunded. If it was applied according to the policy, is there any flexibility to reduce it or turn part of the amount into credit for a future booking?

I'm not asking you to ignore the rules without checking. I want to understand the charge and find a reasonable way forward. Could you explain the available options and send me a written summary after the review? That would help avoid any further misunderstanding.

en.title: 잘 모르는 음악 질문에 답하기
question: What kind of music do you enjoy, and when do you listen to it?
answer: Music isn't an area I follow very closely, so I don't have a detailed list of favorite artists. I tend to think more about the situation than the genre. If I want to relax after a busy day, I'd prefer something that doesn't demand too much attention.

For example, quiet background music could make a short break feel different from the rest of the day. If I'm trying to read something difficult, though, I may prefer silence. I don't want the music competing with the words in front of me.

So I wouldn't call myself a serious music fan, but I can see how music changes the atmosphere. My preference is fairly practical: something that suits the moment. It would be nice to discover a few songs I enjoy, but I don't feel I need to become an expert to appreciate a little music.

en.title: 영화나 공연 경험이 부족할 때
question: What kind of movie would you choose to watch, and why?
answer: I don't have a recent cinema visit that I can describe in detail. These days, I spend more of my free time on exercise, learning, and family, so movies aren't always at the top of my list.

If I were choosing a film, I'd probably be interested in a story about people making difficult decisions. It could involve science, history, or a family facing a major change. What would keep my attention is seeing why the characters choose one path instead of another, rather than simply watching impressive visual effects.

For convenience, watching at home would often suit my schedule. On the other hand, going to a cinema could help me concentrate because I wouldn't be tempted to stop and check something else. So my choice would depend on whether I wanted an easy evening or a more deliberate break from my normal routine.
vocab: at the top of my list

en.title: 관심 있게 본 뉴스 주제
question: What kind of news story has caught your attention recently?
answer: A news topic that keeps catching my attention is AI that helps doctors write clinical notes from conversations. I'm not thinking of one specific headline here. I'm interested in the wider question of how these tools move from demonstrations into everyday use.

When I see a story about a new system, I want to know what happens after the impressive first example. How well does it handle unclear speech? Can the doctor easily correct an error? Does it fit the way a clinic already works? Those questions matter to me because they're close to my own work.

I also try to distinguish what a company hopes to achieve from what has actually been shown. That doesn't make me negative about the technology. It makes me more interested in the details. A news story is useful when it gives me a better question to investigate, not only a reason to feel excited.

en.title: 새로운 사업 아이디어 고민
question: Tell me about an idea you are considering but have not decided on yet.
answer: I'm considering how a property in Yangpyeong might be used for a new business. It previously operated as a café, and I'm interested in whether a different concept could work there. I haven't decided on the final idea.

The exciting part is imagining what the place could become. But the practical questions are more important at this stage. Who would visit? How would they find the entrance? Would people come only once, or would there be a reason to return? I also have a demanding main job, so I need to think carefully about who would manage the place day to day.

I'd rather understand those questions before spending heavily on renovation. A beautiful space alone doesn't guarantee a viable business. For me, this idea is an exercise in connecting what I find interesting with what customers actually need and what I can realistically operate.

en.title: 동료에게 새로운 도구를 제안하기
question: A colleague is hesitant to try a new AI tool. Explain how you would discuss it with them.
answer: I'd start by asking what concerns my colleague most. They might worry about accuracy, extra work, or having to change a familiar routine. If I don't understand that first, a long explanation of the technology probably won't help.

Then I'd suggest a limited evaluation using appropriate sample material. We could choose one task, compare the draft with what we need, and write down the corrections. I wouldn't promise that the tool would solve everything. The aim would be to see whether it offers a useful improvement in that specific situation.

I'd also make it easy to say that the trial wasn't successful. If people feel they must praise a new tool, we won't learn much. My message would be: let's check it together and decide from the result. I think that approach respects professional judgment while still leaving room to try something new.

en.title: AI의 장점과 단점에 대한 의견
question: Do you think AI will make people’s lives better? Explain both benefits and concerns.
answer: Overall, I'm optimistic about AI, but my optimism depends on how we use it. It can reduce repetitive work and help people get started on tasks that once felt too difficult. I've seen how useful that can be when learning or organizing information.

My main concern is overreliance. If an answer sounds polished, people may stop asking whether it's correct. In healthcare, that matters because a small error can have a serious consequence. We need ways to check the output and keep responsibility clear.

I also think access to learning matters. People need opportunities to understand these tools, rather than simply being told to use them. So my answer is yes, AI can improve life, but the benefit isn't automatic. We still need judgment, good working habits, and the willingness to question an answer that looks convincing.

zh.title: 자기소개
question: 请介绍一下你自己。你做什么工作？工作以外喜欢做什么？
qǐng jiè shào yī xià nǐ zì jǐ。 nǐ zuò shén me gōng zuò？ gōng zuò yǐ wài xǐ huan zuò shén me？
answer: 我是韩国人，也是一名家庭医学科医生。现在我在Kakao Healthcare工作，参与开发帮助医生的人工智能工具。我的一项重要工作，是向软件开发人员解释诊室里实际发生的事情。

wǒ shì hán guó rén， yě shì yī míng jiā tíng yī xué kē yī shēng。 xiàn zài wǒ zài Kakao Healthcare gōng zuò， cān yù kāi fā bāng zhù yī shēng de rén gōng zhì néng gōng jù。 wǒ de yī xiàng zhòng yào gōng zuò， shì xiàng ruǎn jiàn kāi fā rén yuán jiě shì zhěn shì lǐ shí jì fā shēng de shì qing。
在这之前，我在中国生活和工作了大约七年。那段经历让我更习惯和不同背景的人合作，也让我一直想把中文学得更好。

zài zhè zhī qián， wǒ zài zhōng guó shēng huó hé gōng zuò le dà yuē qī nián。 nà duàn jīng lì ràng wǒ gèng xí guàn hé bù tóng bèi jǐng de rén hé zuò， yě ràng wǒ yì zhí xiǎng bǎ zhōng wén xué de gèng hǎo。
工作以外，我最近开始打网球，还是个初学者，所以要学的东西很多。我也对投资和学习Python感兴趣。虽然平时比较忙，但是有新的东西可以学习，会让我觉得生活很有意思。

gōng zuò yǐ wài， wǒ zuì jìn kāi shǐ dǎ wǎng qiú， hái shì gè chū xué zhě， suǒ yǐ yào xué de dōng xi hěn duō。 wǒ yě duì tóu zī hé xué xí Python gǎn xìng qù。 suī rán píng shí bǐ jiào máng， dàn shì yǒu xīn de dōng xi kě yǐ xué xí， huì ràng wǒ jué de shēng huó hěn yǒu yì si。
vocab: bù tóng bèi jǐng de rén

zh.title: 현재 업무를 쉽게 설명하기
question: 请具体介绍一下你现在的工作。你主要负责什么？
qǐng jù tǐ jiè shào yī xià nǐ xiàn zài de gōng zuò。 nǐ zhǔ yào fù zé shén me？
answer: 我现在参与开发电子病历里的人工智能工具。电子病历就是医生查看病史、写诊疗记录时使用的软件。我的工作是帮助团队判断，哪些信息在临床上真正重要。

wǒ xiàn zài cān yù kāi fā diàn zi bìng lì lǐ de rén gōng zhì néng gōng jù。 diàn zi bìng lì jiù shì yī shēng chá kàn bìng shǐ、 xiě zhěn liáo jì lù shí shǐ yòng de ruǎn jiàn。 wǒ de gōng zuò shì bāng zhù tuán duì pàn duàn， nǎ xiē xìn xī zài lín chuáng shàng zhēn zhèng zhòng yào。
比如，医生再次见到一位病人之前，可能需要知道上次就诊以后有什么变化。检查结果有没有变差？用药有没有调整？我会把这些问题变成工程师和设计师能够理解的功能需求。

bǐ rú， yī shēng zài cì jiàn dào yī wèi bìng rén zhī qián， kě néng xū yào zhī dào shàng cì jiù zhěn yǐ hòu yǒu shén me biàn huà。 jiǎn chá jié guǒ yǒu méi yǒu biàn chà？ yòng yào yǒu méi yǒu tiáo zhěng？ wǒ huì bǎ zhè xiē wèn tí biàn chéng gōng chéng shī hé shè jì shī néng gòu lǐ jiě de gōng néng xū qiú。
因为要和不同团队合作，沟通占了我很多时间。简单来说，我的角色就是把临床经验和产品开发连接起来。我觉得这份工作很有意义，因为屏幕上的一个小改进，就可能让医生工作得更顺利。

yīn wèi yào hé bù tóng tuán duì hé zuò， gōu tōng zhàn le wǒ hěn duō shí jiān。 jiǎn dān lái shuō， wǒ de jué sè jiù shì bǎ lín chuáng jīng yàn hé chǎn pǐn kāi fā lián jiē qǐ lái。 wǒ jué de zhè fèn gōng zuò hěn yǒu yì yì， yīn wèi píng mù shàng de yí gè xiǎo gǎi jìn， jiù kě néng ràng yī shēng gōng zuò de gèng shùn lì。
vocab: shàng cì jiù zhěn yǐ hòu
把问题转化成功能需求
bǎ wèn tí zhuǎn huà chéng gōng néng xū qiú

zh.title: 평일의 하루
question: 请从早到晚介绍一下你平常的一个工作日。
qǐng cóng zǎo dào wǎn jiè shào yī xià nǐ píng cháng de yí gè gōng zuò rì。
answer: 平常的工作日，我会先看一下日程，确认哪些会议需要准备，哪些事情需要我做决定。有一点时间的话，我也会看看医疗或者人工智能方面的新闻。

píng cháng de gōng zuò rì， wǒ huì xiān kàn yī xià rì chéng， què rèn nǎ xiē huì yì xū yào zhǔn bèi， nǎ xiē shì qing xū yào wǒ zuò jué dìng。 yǒu yì diǎn shí jiān de huà， wǒ yě huì kàn kàn yī liáo huò zhě rén gōng zhì néng fāng miàn de xīn wén。
白天，我经常和医疗、产品、开发团队开会。有时候讨论得很具体，比如病历页面最上面应该显示什么信息；有时候则讨论整个服务的发展方向。不断切换思考角度，其实挺累的。

bái tiān， wǒ jīng cháng hé yī liáo、 chǎn pǐn、 kāi fā tuán duì kāi huì。 yǒu shí hou tǎo lùn de hěn jù tǐ， bǐ rú bìng lì yè miàn zuì shàng miàn yīng gāi xiǎn shì shén me xìn xī； yǒu shí hou zé tǎo lùn zhěng gè fú wù de fā zhǎn fāng xiàng。 bù duàn qiè huàn sī kǎo jiǎo dù， qí shí tǐng lèi de。
晚上，我尽量留一点时间陪家人，也让身体动一动。可能去打网球，做拉伸，或者简单散步。当然，我不是每天都能安排得很好。如果工作结束得晚，我就把计划简化，第二天再继续。

wǎn shàng， wǒ jǐn liàng liú yì diǎn shí jiān péi jiā rén， yě ràng shēn tǐ dòng yī dòng。 kě néng qù dǎ wǎng qiú， zuò lā shēn， huò zhě jiǎn dān sàn bù。 dāng rán， wǒ bú shì měi tiān dōu néng ān pái de hěn hǎo。 rú guǒ gōng zuò jié shù de wǎn， wǒ jiù bǎ jì huà jiǎn huà， dì èr tiān zài jì xù。
vocab: jiè shào yī tiān de ān pái
gōng zuò jié shù de wǎn

zh.title: 기억에 남는 음성 차팅 프로젝트
question: 请介绍一个对你特别有意义的项目。
qǐng jiè shào yí gè duì nǐ tè bié yǒu yì yì de xiàng mù。
answer: 让我印象很深的一个项目，是把医生和病人的对话整理成病历草稿的人工智能工具。医生要花很多时间写记录，所以这是一个非常实际的问题。

ràng wǒ yìn xiàng hěn shēn de yí gè xiàng mù， shì bǎ yī shēng hé bìng rén de duì huà zhěng lǐ chéng bìng lì cǎo gǎo de rén gōng zhì néng gōng jù。 yī shēng yào huā hěn duō shí jiān xiě jì lù， suǒ yǐ zhè shì yí gè fēi cháng shí jì de wèn tí。
难点在于，真实的问诊并不是一段整齐的演讲。病人可能说到一半停下来，突然换个话题，或者提到一种药，却记不清名字。我们需要考虑系统怎么处理这些情况，也需要让医生方便地检查和修改草稿。

nán diǎn zài yú， zhēn shí de wèn zhěn bìng bú shì yī duàn zhěng qí de yǎn jiǎng。 bìng rén kě néng shuō dào yí bàn tíng xià lái， tū rán huàn gè huà tí， huò zhě tí dào yī zhǒng yào， què jì bù qīng míng zi。 wǒ men xū yào kǎo lǜ xì tǒng zěn me chǔ lǐ zhè xiē qíng kuàng， yě xū yào ràng yī shēng fāng biàn de jiǎn chá hé xiū gǎi cǎo gǎo。
我参与梳理这些临床场景，也思考应该怎样评价工具。这个过程让我意识到，演示效果好，并不等于产品可靠。我一直关注的是，它能不能在普通而忙碌的门诊里真正帮上忙。

wǒ cān yù shū lǐ zhè xiē lín chuáng chǎng jǐng， yě sī kǎo yīng gāi zěn yàng píng jià gōng jù。 zhè ge guò chéng ràng wǒ yì shí dào， yǎn shì xiào guǒ hǎo， bìng bù děng yú chǎn pǐn kě kào。 wǒ yì zhí guān zhù de shì， tā néng bù néng zài pǔ tōng ér máng lù de mén zhěn lǐ zhēn zhèng bāng shàng máng。

zh.title: 팀의 의견 차이를 해결한 경험
question: 请说说工作中出现意见分歧的一次经历。你怎么处理的？
qǐng shuō shuō gōng zuò zhōng chū xiàn yì jiàn fēn qí de yī cì jīng lì。 nǐ zěn me chǔ lǐ de？
answer: 我想起一次关于患者摘要页面的讨论。一部分人希望多放一些信息，另一部分人则希望页面更简单。大家一直说信息要重要、操作要方便，但每个人对这些词的理解不一样。

wǒ xiǎng qǐ yī cì guān yú huàn zhě zhāi yào yè miàn de tǎo lùn。 yī bù fèn rén xī wàng duō fàng yī xiē xìn xī， lìng yī bù fèn rén zé xī wàng yè miàn gèng jiǎn dān。 dà jiā yì zhí shuō xìn xī yào zhòng yào、 cāo zuò yào fāng biàn， dàn měi gè rén duì zhè xiē cí de lǐ jiě bù yí yàng。
我建议用一位复诊病人的就诊过程来讨论。医生进诊室之前需要知道什么？哪些细节可以之后再看？有了具体的例子，沟通就容易多了。我们把关键变化和补充资料分开了。

wǒ jiàn yì yòng yī wèi fù zhěn bìng rén de jiù zhěn guò chéng lái tǎo lùn。 yī shēng jìn zhěn shì zhī qián xū yào zhī dào shén me？ nǎ xiē xì jié kě yǐ zhī hòu zài kàn？ yǒu le jù tǐ de lì zi， gōu tōng jiù róng yì duō le。 wǒ men bǎ guān jiàn biàn huà hé bǔ chōng zī liào fēn kāi le。
这样一来，团队就能讨论更清楚的设计方案。这件事说明，意见不同不一定是目标冲突。有时候，大家只是想象了不同的使用场景。

zhè yàng yī lái， tuán duì jiù néng tǎo lùn gèng qīng chǔ de shè jì fāng àn。 zhè jiàn shì shuō míng， yì jiàn bù tóng bù yí dìng shì mù biāo chōng tū。 yǒu shí hou， dà jiā zhǐ shì xiǎng xiàng le bù tóng de shǐ yòng chǎng jǐng。
vocab: yòng jù tǐ lì zi lái tǎo lùn
duì shì qing yǒu bù tóng de lǐ jiě

zh.title: 의료의 과거와 현재
question: 从你开始工作到现在，医疗行业发生了哪些变化？
cóng nǐ kāi shǐ gōng zuò dào xiàn zài， yī liáo háng yè fā shēng le nǎ xiē biàn huà？
answer: 刚开始当医生的时候，我使用的信息大多来自病人到医院就诊的那一刻。我们看病人、查看检查结果，然后制定方案。这些现在仍然重要，但我们也能获得更多日常生活中的信息。

gāng kāi shǐ dāng yī shēng de shí hou， wǒ shǐ yòng de xìn xī dà duō lái zì bìng rén dào yī yuàn jiù zhěn de nà yī kè。 wǒ men kàn bìng rén、 chá kàn jiǎn chá jié guǒ， rán hòu zhì dìng fāng àn。 zhè xiē xiàn zài réng rán zhòng yào， dàn wǒ men yě néng huò dé gèng duō rì cháng shēng huó zhōng de xìn xī。
连续血糖监测就是一个例子。我们看到的不再只是一次血糖结果，而是一段时间里的变化，包括吃饭或者运动以后的情况。数字医疗方面的工作，让我特别关注这种区别。

lián xù xuè táng jiān cè jiù shì yí gè lì zi。 wǒ men kàn dào de bù zài zhǐ shì yī cì xuè táng jié guǒ， ér shì yī duàn shí jiān lǐ de biàn huà， bāo kuò chī fàn huò zhě yùn dòng yǐ hòu de qíng kuàng。 shù zì yī liáo fāng miàn de gōng zuò， ràng wǒ tè bié guān zhù zhè zhǒng qū bié。
不过，数据更多，不代表医疗一定更好。还需要有人解释这些数字的意义，判断哪些变化值得关注。对我来说，最大的变化，是我们可以看到一个更完整的过程，而不只是某一个瞬间。

bù guò， shù jù gèng duō， bù dài biǎo yī liáo yí dìng gèng hǎo。 hái xū yào yǒu rén jiě shì zhè xiē shù zì de yì yì， pàn duàn nǎ xiē biàn huà zhí dé guān zhù。 duì wǒ lái shuō， zuì dà de biàn huà， shì wǒ men kě yǐ kàn dào yí gè gèng wán zhěng de guò chéng， ér bù zhǐ shì mǒu yí gè shùn jiān。
vocab: yī duàn shí jiān lǐ de biàn huà

zh.title: 중국에서 보낸 약 7년
question: 请谈谈你在另一个国家生活的经历。
qǐng tán tán nǐ zài lìng yí gè guó jiā shēng huó de jīng lì。
answer: 我在中国生活和工作了大约七年，在上海、苏州、无锡等地积累了经历。那是我职业生涯中很重要的一段时间，并不是一次短期出差。

wǒ zài zhōng guó shēng huó hé gōng zuò le dà yuē qī nián， zài shàng hǎi、 sū zhōu、 wú xī děng dì jī lèi le jīng lì。 nà shì wǒ zhí yè shēng yá zhōng hěn zhòng yào de yī duàn shí jiān， bìng bú shì yī cì duǎn qī chū chāi。
刚开始，我需要学习的不只是词汇。我还要理解同事怎么解释问题，医院怎么运转，以及怎样和刚认识的人建立信任。医学知识当然有用，但光有医学知识还不够。

gāng kāi shǐ， wǒ xū yào xué xí de bù zhǐ shì cí huì。 wǒ hái yào lǐ jiě tóng shì zěn me jiě shì wèn tí， yī yuàn zěn me yùn zhuàn， yǐ jí zěn yàng hé gāng rèn shi de rén jiàn lì xìn rèn。 yī xué zhī shi dāng rán yǒu yòng， dàn guāng yǒu yī xué zhī shi hái bù gòu。
后来，我越来越愿意先提问，而不是假设自己习惯的方法在哪里都适用。回到韩国以后，我也保留了这个习惯。现在遇到新的团队，我会先了解他们的情况，再提出建议。中国的生活经历让我更灵活，也让我对医疗有了更广的认识。

hòu lái， wǒ yuè lái yuè yuàn yì xiān tí wèn， ér bú shì jiǎ shè zì jǐ xí guàn de fāng fǎ zài nǎ li dōu shì yòng。 huí dào hán guó yǐ hòu， wǒ yě bǎo liú le zhè ge xí guàn。 xiàn zài yù dào xīn de tuán duì， wǒ huì xiān liǎo jiě tā men de qíng kuàng， zài tí chū jiàn yì。 zhōng guó de shēng huó jīng lì ràng wǒ gèng líng huó， yě ràng wǒ duì yī liáo yǒu le gèng guǎng de rèn shi。
vocab: hǎi wài gōng zuò rèn wù

zh.title: 중국 정착 초기의 작은 어려움
question: 请描述一下你刚到国外生活时遇到的一个问题。
qǐng miáo shù yī xià nǐ gāng dào guó wài shēng huó shí yù dào de yí gè wèn tí。
answer: 刚到中国的时候，我开通手机支付遇到了一点困难。我大概知道怎么用，但是注册时卡住了。页面要求填写一些资料，我不确定应该怎么填，所以一直没能完成。

gāng dào zhōng guó de shí hou， wǒ kāi tōng shǒu jī zhī fù yù dào le yì diǎn kùn nán。 wǒ dà gài zhī dào zěn me yòng， dàn shì zhù cè shí kǎ zhù le。 yè miàn yāo qiú tián xiě yī xiē zī liào， wǒ bù què dìng yīng gāi zěn me tián， suǒ yǐ yì zhí méi néng wán chéng。
一开始，我试着把每个词都翻译出来，但还是不明白整个流程。后来，我请一位同事带着我一步一步操作。我们核对了资料，我也把重要的词记了下来。

yī kāi shǐ， wǒ shì zhe bǎ měi gè cí dōu fān yì chū lái， dàn hái shì bù míng bai zhěng gè liú chéng。 hòu lái， wǒ qǐng yī wèi tóng shì dài zhe wǒ yí bù yí bù cāo zuò。 wǒ men hé duì le zī liào， wǒ yě bǎ zhòng yào de cí jì le xià lái。
开通以后，买日常用品就方便多了。这件事让我明白，刚到一个国家生活时，主动求助可以节省很多时间。没有必要从第一天起就要求自己什么都独立解决。

kāi tōng yǐ hòu， mǎi rì cháng yòng pǐn jiù fāng biàn duō le。 zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ míng bai， gāng dào yí gè guó jiā shēng huó shí， zhǔ dòng qiú zhù kě yǐ jié shěng hěn duō shí jiān。 méi yǒu bì yào cóng dì yī tiān qǐ jiù yào qiú zì jǐ shén me dōu dú lì jiě jué。
vocab: dài zhe wǒ yí bù yí bù cāo zuò
shì yìng yí gè xīn de guó jiā

zh.title: 한국과 중국의 업무 경험 비교
question: 请比较一下你在韩国和中国的工作经历。
qǐng bǐ jiào yī xià nǐ zài hán guó hé zhōng guó de gōng zuò jīng lì。
answer: 我确实感受到一些区别，不过不能说一个国家的人都用同一种方式工作。我在中国合作过的一些团队，很愿意先快速尝试，再根据反馈调整。

wǒ què shí gǎn shòu dào yī xiē qū bié， bù guò bù néng shuō yí gè guó jiā de rén dōu yòng tóng yī zhǒng fāng shì gōng zuò。 wǒ zài zhōng guó hé zuò guò de yī xiē tuán duì， hěn yuàn yì xiān kuài sù cháng shì， zài gēn jù fǎn kuì tiáo zhěng。
在另外一些环境里，包括我在韩国的部分经历，大家会先花更多时间把细节讨论清楚，再开始行动。两种方式都有价值。快速尝试可以早点发现问题，认真准备也能避免一些失误。

zài lìng wài yī xiē huán jìng lǐ， bāo kuò wǒ zài hán guó de bù fèn jīng lì， dà jiā huì xiān huā gèng duō shí jiān bǎ xì jié tǎo lùn qīng chǔ， zài kāi shǐ xíng dòng。 liǎng zhǒng fāng shì dōu yǒu jià zhí。 kuài sù cháng shì kě yǐ zǎo diǎn fā xiàn wèn tí， rèn zhēn zhǔn bèi yě néng bì miǎn yī xiē shī wù。
因为我做的是医疗相关工作，所以不能任何时候都只追求速度。页面布局可以小范围试用，但可能影响临床判断的功能，就需要更严格地检查。这些经历让我学会根据具体问题选择合适的方法。

yīn wèi wǒ zuò de shì yī liáo xiāng guān gōng zuò， suǒ yǐ bù néng rèn hé shí hou dōu zhǐ zhuī qiú sù dù。 yè miàn bù jú kě yǐ xiǎo fàn wéi shì yòng， dàn kě néng yǐng xiǎng lín chuáng pàn duàn de gōng néng， jiù xū yào gèng yán gé de jiǎn chá。 zhè xiē jīng lì ràng wǒ xué huì gēn jù jù tǐ wèn tí xuǎn zé hé shì de fāng fǎ。
vocab: gēn jù fǎn kuì tiáo zhěng
kě yǐ bì miǎn de shī wù

zh.title: 외국어 오해를 풀었던 장면
question: 请说说一次因为语言产生误解，以及后来怎么解决的经历。
qǐng shuō shuō yī cì yīn wèi yǔ yán chǎn shēng wù jiě， yǐ jí hòu lái zěn me jiě jué de jīng lì。
answer: 我有一次在会议中误解了完成日期。对方说任务很快就能完成，我以为是这周，后来才发现，对方其实没有答应具体日期。
wǒ yǒu yī cì zài huì yì zhōng wù jiě le wán chéng rì qī。 duì fāng shuō rèn wù hěn kuài jiù néng wán chéng， wǒ yǐ wéi shì zhè zhōu， hòu lái cái fā xiàn， duì fāng qí shí méi yǒu dā yìng jù tǐ rì qī。
因为我已经开始安排下一步，所以有点尴尬。但我没有责怪别人，而是问得更清楚一些：您是指这周五，还是下周某个时间？确认以后，我又复述了一遍日期，并发了一段简短的文字说明。

yīn wèi wǒ yǐ jīng kāi shǐ ān pái xià yī bù， suǒ yǐ yǒu diǎn gān gà。 dàn wǒ méi yǒu zé guài bié rén， ér shì wèn de gèng qīng chǔ yī xiē： nín shì zhǐ zhè zhōu wǔ， hái shì xià zhōu mǒu gè shí jiān？ què rèn yǐ hòu， wǒ yòu fù shù le yī biàn rì qī， bìng fā le yī duàn jiǎn duǎn de wén zì shuō míng。
这个情况说明，听懂词语还不够，还要确认双方到底达成了什么共识。在国际团队里，多问一个确认问题，往往比努力显得口语很流利更有用。

zhè ge qíng kuàng shuō míng， tīng dǒng cí yǔ hái bù gòu， hái yào què rèn shuāng fāng dào dǐ dá chéng le shén me gòng shí。 zài guó jì tuán duì lǐ， duō wèn yí gè què rèn wèn tí， wǎng wǎng bǐ nǔ lì xiǎn de kǒu yǔ hěn liú lì gèng yǒu yòng。
vocab: què rèn duì fāng de yì si
dài zhe wù jiě lí kāi

zh.title: 기억에 남는 도시 우시
question: 请介绍一座对你有特别意义的城市。你为什么记得它？
qǐng jiè shào yī zuò duì nǐ yǒu tè bié yì yì de chéng shì。 nǐ wèi shén me jì de tā？
answer: 无锡是一座对我很有意义的城市，因为我职业生涯中重要的一段时间是在那里度过的。我在国际医疗中心工作，所以我和这座城市的联系，主要来自日常生活和工作，而不是旅游。

wú xī shì yī zuò duì wǒ hěn yǒu yì yì de chéng shì， yīn wèi wǒ zhí yè shēng yá zhōng zhòng yào de yī duàn shí jiān shì zài nà lǐ dù guò de。 wǒ zài guó jì yī liáo zhōng xīn gōng zuò， suǒ yǐ wǒ hé zhè zuò chéng shì de lián xì， zhǔ yào lái zì rì cháng shēng huó hé gōng zuò， ér bú shì lǚ yóu。
想到无锡，我会想到自己怎样学习在不同的环境里运营医疗服务。我需要考虑病人的期待、团队怎么合作，以及怎样把想法变成实际的服务。这些经历让我走出了原来比较单纯的医生角色。

xiǎng dào wú xī， wǒ huì xiǎng dào zì jǐ zěn yàng xué xí zài bù tóng de huán jìng lǐ yùn yíng yī liáo fú wù。 wǒ xū yào kǎo lǜ bìng rén de qī dài、 tuán duì zěn me hé zuò， yǐ jí zěn yàng bǎ xiǎng fǎ biàn chéng shí jì de fú wù。 zhè xiē jīng lì ràng wǒ zǒu chū le yuán lái bǐ jiào dān chún de yī shēng jué sè。
我希望以后有机会回去，看看城市和以前认识的人有什么变化。我想那种感觉会既熟悉又陌生。对我来说，最难忘的城市，往往是让我学到最多东西的地方。

wǒ xī wàng yǐ hòu yǒu jī huì huí qù， kàn kàn chéng shì hé yǐ qián rèn shi de rén yǒu shén me biàn huà。 wǒ xiǎng nà zhǒng gǎn jué huì jì shú xī yòu mò shēng。 duì wǒ lái shuō， zuì nán wàng de chéng shì， wǎng wǎng shì ràng wǒ xué dào zuì duō dōng xi de dì fang。
vocab: jì shú xī yòu mò shēng
chāo chū yuán lái de jué sè

zh.title: 영어 중국어를 함께 공부하는 이유
question: 你在学习什么外语？打算怎么提高？
nǐ zài xué xí shén me wài yǔ？ dǎ suàn zěn me tí gāo？
answer: 我正在准备英语和中文。英语对阅读研究和讨论技术很有用，中文则和我在中国生活工作的经历有很深的联系。我不希望因为现在用得少了，就慢慢失去这种能力。

wǒ zhèng zài zhǔn bèi yīng yǔ hé zhōng wén。 yīng yǔ duì yuè dú yán jiū hé tǎo lùn jì shù hěn yǒu yòng， zhōng wén zé hé wǒ zài zhōng guó shēng huó gōng zuò de jīng lì yǒu hěn shēn de lián xì。 wǒ bù xī wàng yīn wèi xiàn zài yòng de shǎo le， jiù màn màn shī qù zhè zhǒng néng lì。
我的计划是用两种语言准备相同的个人故事，比如工作、网球，或者国外生活。这样，切换语言时，就不用每次重新想一个故事。

wǒ de jì huà shì yòng liǎng zhǒng yǔ yán zhǔn bèi xiāng tóng de gè rén gù shi， bǐ rú gōng zuò、 wǎng qiú， huò zhě guó wài shēng huó。 zhè yàng， qiè huàn yǔ yán shí， jiù bù yòng měi cì chóng xīn xiǎng yí gè gù shi。
不过，我不想逐字翻译，而是希望两种表达都自然。我打算只看几个关键词来讲，再录音，看看哪里容易卡住。对我来说，每次练习一小段，比等到整个下午都有空更现实。目标是更轻松地表达自己的想法。

bù guò， wǒ bù xiǎng zhú zì fān yì， ér shì xī wàng liǎng zhǒng biǎo dá dōu zì rán。 wǒ dǎ suàn zhǐ kàn jǐ gè guān jiàn cí lái jiǎng， zài lù yīn， kàn kàn nǎ lǐ róng yì kǎ zhù。 duì wǒ lái shuō， měi cì liàn xí yī xiǎo duàn， bǐ děng dào zhěng gè xià wǔ dōu yǒu kòng gèng xiàn shí。 mù biāo shì gèng qīng sōng de biǎo dá zì jǐ de xiǎng fǎ。
vocab: 在忙碌的日程里安排时间
zài máng lù de rì chéng lǐ ān pái shí jiān
biǎo dá zì jǐ de xiǎng fǎ

zh.title: 2027년 박사과정 진학
question: 请说说你在学习或者职业方面的一个重要计划。
qǐng shuō shuō nǐ zài xué xí huò zhě zhí yè fāng miàn de yí gè zhòng yào jì huà。
answer: 我已经被韩国科学技术院的博士项目录取，计划在二零二七年开始学习。我感兴趣的方向是人工智能和医疗。同时，我也打算继续工作，所以时间管理会是一个很大的挑战。

wǒ yǐ jīng bèi hán guó kē xué jì shù yuàn de bó shì xiàng mù lù qǔ， jì huà zài èr líng èr qī nián kāi shǐ xué xí。 wǒ gǎn xìng qù de fāng xiàng shì rén gōng zhì néng hé yī liáo。 tóng shí， wǒ yě dǎ suàn jì xù gōng zuò， suǒ yǐ shí jiān guǎn lǐ huì shì yí gè hěn dà de tiǎo zhàn。
我想重新学习，是因为工作中经常遇到光靠实践经验无法充分回答的问题。比如，怎样把复杂的病历变成真正帮助医生的信息？我希望通过更扎实的研究训练来探索这些问题。

wǒ xiǎng chóng xīn xué xí， shì yīn wèi gōng zuò zhōng jīng cháng yù dào guāng kào shí jiàn jīng yàn wú fǎ chōng fèn huí dá de wèn tí。 bǐ rú， zěn yàng bǎ fù zá de bìng lì biàn chéng zhēn zhèng bāng zhù yī shēng de xìn xī？ wǒ xī wàng tōng guò gèng zhā shí de yán jiū xùn liàn lái tàn suǒ zhè xiē wèn tí。
我很期待重新成为学生，也知道这个过程不会轻松。我需要固定留出阅读、技术学习和研究的时间。对我来说，读博士是把临床、商业经验和人工智能研究进一步连接起来的机会。

wǒ hěn qī dài chóng xīn chéng wéi xué shēng， yě zhī dào zhè ge guò chéng bú huì qīng sōng。 wǒ xū yào gù dìng liú chū yuè dú、 jì shù xué xí hé yán jiū de shí jiān。 duì wǒ lái shuō， dú bó shì shì bǎ lín chuáng、 shāng yè jīng yàn hé rén gōng zhì néng yán jiū jìn yí bù lián jiē qǐ lái de jī huì。
vocab: yǐ jīng bèi xiàng mù lù qǔ
计划在二零二七年开始
jì huà zài èr líng èr qī nián kāi shǐ
jiān gù xué xí hé gōng zuò

zh.title: 초보자로서 Python 배우기
question: 请介绍一项你正在学习的新技能。你觉得哪里比较难？
qǐng jiè shào yī xiàng nǐ zhèng zài xué xí de xīn jì néng。 nǐ jué de nǎ lǐ bǐ jiào nán？
answer: 我刚开始学习Python，还是初学者。长期目标是用它做数据分析，尤其是研究公司和投资机会。我也希望能更直接地理解工作中的技术讨论。

wǒ gāng kāi shǐ xué xí Python， hái shì chū xué zhě。 zhǎng qī mù biāo shì yòng tā zuò shù jù fēn xī， yóu qí shì yán jiū gōng sī hé tóu zī jī huì。 wǒ yě xī wàng néng gèng zhí jiē de lǐ jiě gōng zuò zhōng de jì shù tǎo lùn。
困难在于，知道自己想分析什么，和知道代码应该怎么写，是两回事。一个小错误就可能让程序停下来，而屏幕上的提示也不一定容易理解。所以我需要耐心，一步一步解决问题。

kùn nán zài yú， zhī dào zì jǐ xiǎng fēn xī shén me， hé zhī dào dài mǎ yīng gāi zěn me xiě， shì liǎng huí shì。 yí gè xiǎo cuò wù jiù kě néng ràng chéng xù tíng xià lái， ér píng mù shàng de tí shì yě bù yí dìng róng yì lǐ jiě。 suǒ yǐ wǒ xū yào nài xīn， yí bù yí bù jiě jué wèn tí。
对我来说，比较现实的起点是一张简单的数据表：先读取数据，再计算几个数值，最后画一张清楚的图。我不期待一下子成为专家，但希望以后能亲自验证想法，而不是完全依赖别人的分析。

duì wǒ lái shuō， bǐ jiào xiàn shí de qǐ diǎn shì yī zhāng jiǎn dān de shù jù biǎo： xiān dú qǔ shù jù， zài jì suàn jǐ gè shù zhí， zuì hòu huà yī zhāng qīng chǔ de tú。 wǒ bù qī dài yī xià zi chéng wéi zhuān jiā， dàn xī wàng yǐ hòu néng qīn zì yàn zhèng xiǎng fǎ， ér bú shì wán quán yī lài bié rén de fēn xī。
vocab: qīn zì yàn zhèng xiǎng fǎ

zh.title: 취미로서 투자 공부
question: 空闲的时候，你喜欢研究什么？
kòng xián de shí hou， nǐ xǐ huan yán jiū shén me？
answer: 空闲的时候，我喜欢研究投资。赚钱当然是吸引我的一个原因，但我也想理解，为什么有些行业发展得很好，有些却遇到困难。投资给了我一个研究世界变化的实际理由。

kòng xián de shí hou， wǒ xǐ huan yán jiū tóu zī。 zhuàn qián dāng rán shì xī yǐn wǒ de yí gè yuán yīn， dàn wǒ yě xiǎng lǐ jiě， wéi shén me yǒu xiē háng yè fā zhǎn de hěn hǎo， yǒu xiē què yù dào kùn nán。 tóu zī gěi le wǒ yí gè yán jiū shì jiè biàn huà de shí jì lǐ yóu。
我特别关注人工智能、半导体和医疗健康。看到一项很有前景的技术时，我会问，客户到底愿意为什么付钱，公司又怎样赚钱。故事讲得好，不代表生意一定好。

wǒ tè bié guān zhù rén gōng zhì néng、 bàn dǎo tǐ hé yī liáo jiàn kāng。 kàn dào yī xiàng hěn yǒu qián jǐng de jì shù shí， wǒ huì wèn， kè hù dào dǐ yuàn yì wèi shén me fù qián， gōng sī yòu zěn yàng zhuàn qián。 gù shi jiǎng de hǎo， bù dài biǎo shēng yì yí dìng hǎo。
最难的部分是面对不确定性。即使认真研究，也可能判断错误。所以我会尽量分清楚，哪些是已知的事实，哪些只是自己的假设。投资不总是让人放松，但它让我保持好奇，也提醒我反思自己的判断。

zuì nán de bù fèn shì miàn duì bù què dìng xìng。 jí shǐ rèn zhēn yán jiū， yě kě néng pàn duàn cuò wù。 suǒ yǐ wǒ huì jǐn liàng fēn qīng chǔ， nǎ xiē shì yǐ zhī de shì shí， nǎ xiē zhǐ shì zì jǐ de jiǎ shè。 tóu zī bù zǒng shì ràng rén fàng sōng， dàn tā ràng wǒ bǎo chí hào qí， yě tí xǐng wǒ fǎn sī zì jǐ de pàn duàn。
vocab: miàn duì bù què dìng xìng
fǎn sī zì jǐ de pàn duàn

zh.title: 최근 깊이 살펴본 산업
question: 请说说你最近花时间研究的一个话题。
qǐng shuō shuō nǐ zuì jìn huā shí jiān yán jiū de yí gè huà tí。
answer: 最近，我对造船行业比较感兴趣。听起来好像离医学很远，但我喜欢研究技术、商业和全球贸易交织在一起的话题。
zuì jìn， wǒ duì zào chuán háng yè bǐ jiào gǎn xìng qù。 tīng qǐ lái hǎo xiàng lí yī xué hěn yuǎn， dàn wǒ xǐ huan yán jiū jì shù、 shāng yè hé quán qiú mào yì jiāo zhī zài yì qǐ de huà tí。
我正在思考的一个问题是，如果很多旧船需要更换，但船厂不能马上扩大产量，会发生什么？需求强只是其中一部分，还要考虑生产能力、交付时间、成本，以及环保要求的变化。所以事情没有一个简单的增长故事那么容易。

wǒ zhèng zài sī kǎo de yí gè wèn tí shì， rú guǒ hěn duō jiù chuán xū yào gēng huàn， dàn chuán chǎng bù néng mǎ shàng kuò dà chǎn liàng， huì fā shēng shén me？ xū qiú qiáng zhǐ shì qí zhōng yī bù fèn， hái yào kǎo lǜ shēng chǎn néng lì、 jiāo fù shí jiān、 chéng běn， yǐ jí huán bǎo yāo qiú de biàn huà。 suǒ yǐ shì qing méi yǒu yí gè jiǎn dān de zēng zhǎng gù shi nà me róng yì。
我喜欢比较几种可能的情况，而不是只相信一个预测。如果需求持续强劲会怎样？如果订单减少又会怎样？我还没有最终答案。研究专业之外的领域，也让我意识到自己还有很多东西需要学习。

wǒ xǐ huan bǐ jiào jǐ zhǒng kě néng de qíng kuàng， ér bú shì zhǐ xiāng xìn yí gè yù cè。 rú guǒ xū qiú chí xù qiáng jìng huì zěn yàng？ rú guǒ dìng dān jiǎn shǎo yòu huì zěn yàng？ wǒ hái méi yǒu zuì zhōng dá àn。 yán jiū zhuān yè zhī wài de lǐng yù， yě ràng wǒ yì shí dào zì jǐ hái yǒu hěn duō dōng xi xū yào xué xí。
vocab: bǐ jiào kě néng de jié guǒ
zhǐ yī lài yí gè yù cè

zh.title: 읽고 싶은 역사책과 독서 습관
question: 你对什么类型的书感兴趣？请介绍一本你想读的书。
nǐ duì shén me lèi xíng de shū gǎn xìng qù？ qǐng jiè shào yī běn nǐ xiǎng dú de shū。
answer: 我对帮助理解个人和社会变化的书比较感兴趣。尤其是历史，因为它能提供比每日新闻更长远的视角。
wǒ duì bāng zhù lǐ jiě gè rén hé shè huì biàn huà de shū bǐ jiào gǎn xìng qù。 yóu qí shì lì shǐ， yīn wèi tā néng tí gōng bǐ měi rì xīn wén gèng cháng yuǎn de shì jiǎo。
我想多花一点时间读的一本书，是杜兰特夫妇的《历史的教训》。我对书里关于人类行为和社会变化的问题很感兴趣。我不认为历史能提供准确预测未来的公式，但它可以帮助我们把今天的事情放到更大的背景里理解。

wǒ xiǎng duō huā yì diǎn shí jiān dú de yī běn shū， shì dù lán tè fū fù de 《lì shǐ de jiào xùn》。 wǒ duì shū lǐ guān yú rén lèi xíng wéi hé shè huì biàn huà de wèn tí hěn gǎn xìng qù。 wǒ bù rèn wéi lì shǐ néng tí gōng zhǔn què yù cè wèi lái de gōng shì， dàn tā kě yǐ bāng zhù wǒ men bǎ jīn tiān de shì qing fàng dào gèng dà de bèi jǐng lǐ lǐ jiě。
平时比较忙，我不一定能连续读很久。对我来说，一个可行的方法是先读一小段，再写下一个问题，然后想想它和工作或者投资研究有什么联系。我希望阅读能影响我的思考方式，而不只是增加读过的书的数量。

píng shí bǐ jiào máng， wǒ bù yí dìng néng lián xù dú hěn jiǔ。 duì wǒ lái shuō， yí gè kě xíng de fāng fǎ shì xiān dú yī xiǎo duàn， zài xiě xià yí gè wèn tí， rán hòu xiǎng xiǎng tā hé gōng zuò huò zhě tóu zī yán jiū yǒu shén me lián xì。 wǒ xī wàng yuè dú néng yǐng xiǎng wǒ de sī kǎo fāng shì， ér bù zhǐ shì zēng jiā dú guò de shū de shù liàng。
vocab: gèng cháng yuǎn de shì jiǎo
fàng dào bèi jǐng lǐ lǐ jiě
xiě xià yí gè wèn tí

zh.title: 앞으로 5년의 목표
question: 五年以后，你希望自己是什么样的状态？
wǔ nián yǐ hòu， nǐ xī wàng zì jǐ shì shén me yàng de zhuàng tài？
answer: 五年以后，我希望自己的医生经验和人工智能工作能够结合得更深入。我做过临床工作，在中国参与过医疗服务，也在韩国从事数字医疗。现在，我希望把这些经历连接得更完整。

wǔ nián yǐ hòu， wǒ xī wàng zì jǐ de yī shēng jīng yàn hé rén gōng zhì néng gōng zuò néng gòu jié hé de gēng shēn rù。 wǒ zuò guò lín chuáng gōng zuò， zài zhōng guó cān yù guò yī liáo fú wù， yě zài hán guó cóng shì shù zì yī liáo。 xiàn zài， wǒ xī wàng bǎ zhè xiē jīng lì lián jiē de gèng wán zhěng。
一个目标是在博士研究中取得实质进展，另一个目标是帮助开发医生真正愿意使用的工具，因为它们确实解决了问题。相比一场听起来很精彩的演讲，我更希望看到产品改善日常工作。

yí gè mù biāo shì zài bó shì yán jiū zhōng qǔ dé shí zhì jìn zhǎn， lìng yí gè mù biāo shì bāng zhù kāi fā yī shēng zhēn zhèng yuàn yì shǐ yòng de gōng jù， yīn wèi tā men què shí jiě jué le wèn tí。 xiāng bǐ yī cháng tīng qǐ lái hěn jīng cǎi de yǎn jiǎng， wǒ gèng xī wàng kàn dào chǎn pǐn gǎi shàn rì cháng gōng zuò。
我也想保持健康，享受这个过程。网球和耐力运动方面的兴趣，也是这个目标的一部分。计划可能会变化，所以我并不只盯着某个职位。我更在意持续学习，并成为能把不同领域连接起来的人。

wǒ yě xiǎng bǎo chí jiàn kāng， xiǎng shòu zhè ge guò chéng。 wǎng qiú hé nài lì yùn dòng fāng miàn de xìng qù， yě shì zhè ge mù biāo de yī bù fèn。 jì huà kě néng huì biàn huà， suǒ yǐ wǒ bìng bù zhǐ dīng zhe mǒu gè zhí wèi。 wǒ gèng zài yì chí xù xué xí， bìng chéng wéi néng bǎ bù tóng lǐng yù lián jiē qǐ lái de rén。
vocab: qǔ dé shí zhì jìn zhǎn
zhí zhuó yú mǒu gè zhí wèi
xiǎng shòu zhè ge guò chéng

zh.title: 최근 시작한 테니스
question: 你最近对什么运动感兴趣？请具体说一说。
nǐ zuì jìn duì shén me yùn dòng gǎn xìng qù？ qǐng jù tǐ shuō yī shuō。
answer: 我最近开始对网球感兴趣。二零二六年夏天才开始打，所以现在还是初学者。我喜欢它的一点，是打球时必须专注在眼前。
wǒ zuì jìn kāi shǐ duì wǎng qiú gǎn xìng qù。 èr líng èr liù nián xià tiān cái kāi shǐ dǎ， suǒ yǐ xiàn zài hái shì chū xué zhě。 wǒ xǐ huan tā de yì diǎn， shì dǎ qiú shí bì xū zhuān zhù zài yǎn qián。
工作的时候，我脑子里常常同时想着好几个问题。但在球场上，下一个球飞过来，就必须马上注意。即使只是简单对打，也需要掌握时间、脚步和击球力量。自己打起来，比看熟练的人打要难得多。

gōng zuò de shí hou， wǒ nǎo zi lǐ cháng cháng tóng shí xiǎng zhe hǎo jǐ gè wèn tí。 dàn zài qiú chǎng shàng， xià yí gè qiú fēi guò lái， jiù bì xū mǎ shàng zhù yì。 jí shǐ zhǐ shì jiǎn dān duì dǎ， yě xū yào zhǎng wò shí jiān、 jiǎo bù hé jī qiú lì liàng。 zì jǐ dǎ qǐ lái， bǐ kàn shú liàn de rén dǎ yào nán de duō。
我还找过可以对着墙练习的地方，没有球友的时候也能练。我不期待马上打得很好。目前只要击球更稳定、移动更舒服一点，我就会觉得有进步，也有动力继续。

wǒ hái zhǎo guò kě yǐ duì zhe qiáng liàn xí de dì fang， méi yǒu qiú yǒu de shí hou yě néng liàn。 wǒ bù qī dài mǎ shàng dǎ de hěn hǎo。 mù qián zhǐ yào jī qiú gèng wěn dìng、 yí dòng gèng shū fu yì diǎn， wǒ jiù huì jué de yǒu jìn bù， yě yǒu dòng lì jì xù。

zh.title: 첫 테니스 레슨의 작은 깨달음
question: 请说说学习运动时一次难忘的经历。
qǐng shuō shuō xué xí yùn dòng shí yī cì nán wàng de jīng lì。
answer: 让我印象很深的一次经历，是刚开始学网球时的一堂课。当时我总想把球打得更有力，以为力量大就会打得好。结果球一直往不该去的方向飞，我也越来越着急。

ràng wǒ yìn xiàng hěn shēn de yī cì jīng lì， shì gāng kāi shǐ xué wǎng qiú shí de yī táng kè。 dāng shí wǒ zǒng xiǎng bǎ qiú dǎ de gèng yǒu lì， yǐ wéi lì liàng dà jiù huì dǎ de hǎo。 jié guǒ qiú yì zhí wǎng bù gāi qù de fāng xiàng fēi， wǒ yě yuè lái yuè zháo jí。
教练让我慢一点，先注意脚步。我把挥拍动作缩小，也尽量提前站好位置。试了几次以后，终于能比较稳定地对打几个球了。虽然不是什么精彩的击球，但感觉比猛打一球、接着失误三次好多了。

jiào liàn ràng wǒ màn yì diǎn， xiān zhù yì jiǎo bù。 wǒ bǎ huī pāi dòng zuò suō xiǎo， yě jǐn liàng tí qián zhàn hǎo wèi zhì。 shì le jǐ cì yǐ hòu， zhōng yú néng bǐ jiào wěn dìng de duì dǎ jǐ gè qiú le。 suī rán bú shì shén me jīng cǎi de jī qiú， dàn gǎn jué bǐ měng dǎ yī qiú、 jiē zhe shī wù sān cì hǎo duō le。
我松了一口气，因为终于知道自己应该先练什么。这次经历让我明白，初学的时候，把简单的动作做稳定，比急着表现得很熟练更有用。学外语也是一样。

wǒ sōng le yì kǒu qì， yīn wèi zhōng yú zhī dào zì jǐ yīng gāi xiān liàn shén me。 zhè cì jīng lì ràng wǒ míng bai， chū xué de shí hou， bǎ jiǎn dān de dòng zuò zuò wěn dìng， bǐ jí zhe biǎo xiàn de hěn shú liàn gèng yǒu yòng。 xué wài yǔ yě shì yī yàng。
vocab: tí qián zhàn hǎo wèi zhì
bǎ huī pāi dòng zuò suō xiǎo

zh.title: 운동 습관의 변화
question: 你的运动习惯这些年有什么变化？
nǐ de yùn dòng xí guàn zhè xiē nián yǒu shén me biàn huà？
answer: 我对运动的看法发生了一些变化。以前更容易关注一次训练有多累，现在更在意能不能恢复好，能不能长期坚持。
wǒ duì yùn dòng de kàn fǎ fā shēng le yī xiē biàn huà。 yǐ qián gèng róng yì guān zhù yī cì xùn liàn yǒu duō lèi， xiàn zài gèng zài yì néng bù néng huī fù hǎo， néng bù néng cháng qī jiān chí。
